contributions.text: To ask His Majesty’s Government what steps they are taking to support inclusion of instruction about soils at all levels of the education system, including undergraduate and post-graduate, and what steps they are taking to increase the level of soil science research.
contributions.name: Baroness Bennett of Manor Castle

contributions.text: My Lords, I begin with thanks to the British Society of Soil Science, the National Trust and the charity Buglife for their assistance in preparation for this debate. I also thank the noble Baroness, Lady Smith of Malvern, who gave me one starting point: her response yesterday to my Written Question about the current number of postgraduate soil science students. The Answer was that, in total, at UK HE providers, there are 45, of whom only 15 are on research courses—fifteen people. Two separate searches of UK job sites this year found more than 100 vacancies for soil scientists each time. The other starting point was an event held last month by the British Society of Soil Science, an attempt to kick-start discussion about what can only be described as the collapse of soil science education and research in the UK. It was under Chatham House rules, so I cannot attribute this, but a sentence that stuck with me was, “We employed the last soil science PhD”.
